Read detections from an OTN, GLATOS, InnovaSea or detqc file

Source: R/read_detections.R
read_detections.Rd

Reads one or more detection files into a data frame with the column names of the positionR table contract. The column map for each format is a CSV file in the package (see column_map()), and read_detections() takes its names, types and time zones from it. Columns are found by name, so their order in the file does not matter. Where a map lists two source columns for one target, the first that holds a value is used, row by row.

Usage

read_detections(
  file,
  format = c("auto", "otn", "glatos", "vue", "vdat", "detqc"),
  col_map = NULL,
  tz = NULL,
  cut = NULL
)

Arguments

file

Path to a detection file, or several paths. Several files are read one by one and stacked, with their name in the column source_file; columns one file lacks are NA in its rows.

format

One of "auto", "otn", "glatos", "vue", "vdat" or "detqc". The default, the full vector, reads as "auto".

col_map

Optional column map. A data frame, or the path to a CSV file, laid out as column_map() describes, replaces the packaged map. Pairs written as c(target = "source") are merged into the format's map: each replaces the rows of its target, and the other targets are read as the format reads them. A pair whose column is not in the file stops; column_map() gives the order in which a pair names the columns the format joins, as GLATOS joins two for transmitter.

tz

Optional time zone, from OlsonNames(), for stamps that carry no zone of their own. NULL uses the zone in the column map (UTC for every packaged format).

cut

Optional list that keeps part of each file as it is read, before the files are stacked, so memory holds one whole file at a time and not the whole set: from and to, date-times in UTC (POSIXct, or text such as "2024-06-03"), keep from <= datetime < to; transmitters, a character vector, keeps those codes. On a study of several gigabytes of VDAT files, a cut to one month and one species bounds the memory by the largest file instead of every row.

Value

A data frame with datetime, receiver_serial, transmitter, animal_id, station_id, sensor_raw, sensor_value, sensor_unit, the other mapped columns and the unmapped ones. The attribute source is a list with one record per file, also for one file: the file, format, OTN extract kind, time zone, rows read and kept, rows dropped as cut (cut_rows) or outside cut (rows_outside_cut), and the map rows used.

Details

Formats. "auto" reads the header and picks one of:

  • "otn": an OTN detection extract, CSV or parquet, in the column names OTN used from June 2025 or before. OTN publishes six kinds of extract. Three hold detections of animals or tags and are read: matched to animals (catalogNumber names the animal), mapped to other trackers ("qualified") and unqualified. The sentinel extracts are read the same way. In every extract but the matched one catalogNumber names a detection or a tag, so animal_id is NA: these extracts are read with the rows of column_map("detections", "otn_qualified"), and a full map that reads animal_id from catalogNumber stops on them. The extract matched to external partners holds counts of possible detections, and stops read_detections(). A matched extract also holds one release record per animal (receiver "release"); these are not detections, so they are set aside in the attribute releases and counted.

  • "glatos": a GLATOS detection export.

  • "vue": a VUE or Fathom detection export with the VUE header.

  • "vdat": a Fathom VDAT CSV (VEMCO DATA LOG), from the receiver's VRL or VDAT file. DET and DET_SENS records are read; a DET record that repeats a DET_SENS record is dropped and counted. The receiver's own transmitter settings (CFG_TRANSMITTER: code, power level, delays) are in the attribute receiver_transmitters.

  • "detqc": a table with detqc's own column names (datetime, receiver_serial, transmitter and the others below), such as a detset's detections written with write.csv(). A blank-headed first column of unique whole numbers, the row names write.csv() writes by default, is dropped.

"auto" picks the format whose map finds the most of datetime, transmitter and receiver_serial in the header, and needs two. When a file read with no col_map in the guessed format then stops, the error first names that format and the columns the guess rests on. With a full map as col_map, a file that no format fits is read by the map alone, and the attribute source gives its format as "col_map".

Time. Every datetime is returned in UTC. OTN, GLATOS and VUE exports are written in UTC. A header that states an offset, such as "Date and Time (UTC-04:00)", and a stamp that carries one, such as "2024-05-01T10:00:00-04:00", are read at that offset. In a VDAT file the Time column is the receiver's corrected time at the Time Offset (h) of its row; where Time is blank the uncorrected Device Time (UTC) is used. tz reads stamps that carry no zone in another zone, for a file exported in local time.

Sensors. Readings with no unit, or the unit "ADC", are raw counts. They go to sensor_raw and leave sensor_value and sensor_unit as NA until calibrate_sensors() converts them. Readings with a physical unit go to sensor_value, with the unit in sensor_unit ("m", "C" or "m/s2"). A unit in brackets, such as "[m]", reads as the unit inside them. In an OTN extract a sensor detection's code is sensorName, so transmitter takes it, and tag_name keeps the pinger code OTN files it under.

Receivers. A receiver written as model and serial, such as "VR2Tx-480013", is split: receiver_serial holds the serial, "480013", as deployment sheets write it, and receiver_model holds the model. Only a known receiver family (VR, HR, TBR and others) followed by three or more digits is split, so OTN collector numbers such as "HFX068-00348-1" stay whole.

Columns the map does not name are kept after the contract columns, with their names in lower case and underscores. No row is removed, except the OTN release records and repeated VDAT records named above.

Raw receiver files. A receiver's own VRL or VDAT file is binary and a zip archive holds other files, so neither is read: each stops with a message that says to export the receiver file to a VDAT CSV with Fathom Connect, or to unzip the archive. OTN publishes some extracts zipped.

Damaged files. A file of 0 bytes stops read_detections() with its name. A file whose last line stops part-way through a row, with no line end, as an interrupted copy or sync leaves it, has that row dropped with a warning. A last row cut short that still ends in a line end has its first fields and NA in the rest. Rows at the end of a file with no transmitter, receiver_serial or station_id are dropped with one warning that counts them, and cut_rows in the source record counts them too. A VDAT file that declares an EVENT_OFFLOAD record but holds none is named in a warning, because its end may be missing.

Compressed files. A gzip, bzip2 or xz file is read through R's own decoder, so R.utils is not needed, and a gzip file of several members reads as one text. Its decompressed text is tested for a cut row in the same way, and its stream for its end record. A stream that stops before its end gives a warning that names the file and counts the rows read; a part-row at the cut is dropped. Padding after a gzip stream, zero bytes as a tape or tar block leaves or a run of 4 or more 0xFF bytes, is not read as text: a whole stream so padded reads with no warning, and one cut in its text is read to the cut, with the warning. A whole stream followed by 1 to 3 bytes of any value also reads with no warning. 4 or more bytes that are not padding give the warning although every row was read, and stop the reader with an error when they begin as a gzip member does (1f 8b). bzip2 decodes whole blocks of up to 900 kB of text, so a small bzip2 file cut part-way holds no row, and stops with an error that names the file.

A gzip stream ends in an 8-byte record: a check value, then the length of the text. A file cut inside its end record stops with an error that names the file; a file that lacks the whole record stops, or reads every row and warns, by how the stream was written. Bytes after a cut inside the check value change nothing. A file cut inside the length stops too when fewer bytes follow the cut than it lacks. When at least as many follow, it reads every row. It gives no warning when those bytes are 4 or more bytes of padding, and otherwise it can warn that rows are missing although none are.

See also

read_deployments(), read_animals(), detset()

Examples

vue_file <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_vue.csv", package = "detqc")
vue_detections <- read_detections(vue_file)
head(vue_detections)
#>              datetime receiver_serial    transmitter animal_id station_id
#> 1 2024-06-03 00:00:26            R013 A69-1601-61001      <NA>       S013
#> 2 2024-06-03 00:03:15            R013 A69-1601-61001      <NA>       S013
#> 3 2024-06-03 00:05:29            R013 A69-1601-61001      <NA>       S013
#> 4 2024-06-03 00:07:41            R013 A69-1601-61001      <NA>       S013
#> 5 2024-06-03 00:09:53            R013 A69-1601-61001      <NA>       S013
#> 6 2024-06-03 00:17:37            R013 A69-1601-61001      <NA>       S013
#>   sensor_raw sensor_value sensor_unit deploy_lat deploy_lon
#> 1         NA           NA        <NA>         NA         NA
#> 2         NA           NA        <NA>         NA         NA
#> 3         NA           NA        <NA>         NA         NA
#> 4         NA           NA        <NA>         NA         NA
#> 5         NA           NA        <NA>         NA         NA
#> 6         NA           NA        <NA>         NA         NA
#>   transmitter_serial
#> 1                 NA
#> 2                 NA
#> 3                 NA
#> 4                 NA
#> 5                 NA
#> 6                 NA
attr(vue_detections, "source")[[1]]$format
#> [1] "vue"

# A Fathom VDAT CSV
vdat_file <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_vdat.csv", package = "detqc")
vdat_detections <- read_detections(vdat_file, "vdat")
#> stoney_vdat.csv: 5 DET records repeat a DET_SENS record and were dropped.
table(vdat_detections$transmitter)
#> 
#> A69-1601-61001 A69-1601-61004 A69-9002-61002 A69-9002-61003 
#>             31             55             54             10 
attr(vdat_detections, "receiver_transmitters")
#>   receiver_serial receiver_model            datetime    transmitter
#> 1            R011       VR2Tx-69 2024-06-01 14:00:00 A69-1601-60011
#>   power_level min_delay max_delay
#> 1   VERY_HIGH       540       660
